kids.name: caption
kids.chars: Research questions and pre-registered hypotheses (memo §2); every status untested

kids.name: value
kids.chars: How does a trader want the ladder to re-centre: "auto-follow vs free-scroll vs lock"?

kids.name: value
kids.chars: H1: auto-follow with an edge band is preferred; centre lock suits only a trader who does not click the ladder (untested, unquantified)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: auto-follow default, free-scroll visible, centre lock a setting

kids.name: value
kids.chars: Does the heatmap belong behind the ladder, beside it, or behind the chart?

kids.name: value
kids.chars: H2: beside the ladder reads faster than behind it, because sizes and own orders stay on a constant surface

kids.name: value
kids.chars: beside on SCR-050; the chart-mounted heatmap is its own surface

q/value.chars: What must "liquidity was pulled" look like so a trader trusts it?

h/value.chars: H3: a pulled mark is trusted only when it is visibly different from a consumed one and says it is an estimate

lean/value.chars: a pattern carrier plus the estimated word; never hue alone

q/value.chars: Which depth tier do people reach for, and what do they expect to lose when the app sheds one?

h/value.chars: H4: 200 is the working tier; on a shed traders expect to lose the far walls and cannot name the cumulative-depth loss unaided

lean/value.chars: 200 default; the notice names the loss

q/value.chars: Do the heatmap and the ladder share one price axis, or can they be zoomed independently?

h/value.chars: H5: an independent zoom breaks the row-by-row read across the two

lean/value.chars: one locked price axis on SCR-050

kids.name: scale
kids.chars: Severity: Blocker (a trade or a read goes wrong) · Major (a read is slow or doubtful) · Minor.

kids.name: value
kids.chars: (heuristic) The plan already implies three centring states: the story wants a re-centre "without jitter on every tick", the hotkey line has a resume, and the sign-off checklist names all three. A design that draws one state leaves the other two to the build.

kids.name: value
kids.chars: "the ladder recentres when price approaches the edge, without jitter on every tick" (11:1982) · "Space = re-centre + resume auto-follow" (14:1214) · "centred / free-scroll / recentre behaviour drawn" (14:1224)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: (heuristic) A centre lock (the mark pinned to one row) moves every row whenever the price moves. On a click-to-trade grid the row under the pointer then changes between aiming and clicking: a misplaced order, not a slow read.

kids.name: value
kids.chars: "book updates at up to 20 Hz must render within one frame" (14:1218) · click a column = a limit order at that price (14:1214)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: (heuristic) When a trader scrolls away the ladder must say it has stopped following; a still ladder otherwise reads as a quiet market. 05 §7 also asks for a pause control on any auto-moving content over 5 s, which the free-scroll state serves as.

kids.name: value
kids.chars: "any auto-moving content lasting >5s has an accessible pause control" (05:217) · C centres on the mark (14:1214)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: (heuristic) Drawing the heatmap behind the ladder puts a moving colour ramp under the size numbers and the own-order cells, so their contrast changes with the liquidity under them, and it collides with the sign-off item that own orders are never obscured. The catalogue's own drawing already puts the heatmap beside the ladder.

kids.name: value
kids.chars: "see resting liquidity over time (heatmap) behind a clickable price ladder for precise execution" (14:1192) · the ASCII's heatmap (time ->) and ladder columns (14:1198) · "own-order markers never obscured by heatmap" (14:1221)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: (heuristic) SCR-050's heatmap and the chart-mounted heatmap answer different questions on different time axes: SCR-050's columns are time (100 ms each), the chart's sit under candles on bar space. One placement rule cannot serve both.

kids.name: value
kids.chars: "overlays needing true time (heatmap columns, session shading) map through time" (26:225) · "behind/under the CandleSeries canvas, synced to the shared price/time axes" (15:2518)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: (heuristic) The probe "where is real support?" is answered by reading one price row across the heatmap into the ladder. If the heatmap could zoom on its own, its rows would stop lining up with the ladder's, and the read across breaks.

kids.name: value
kids.chars: rows are integer tick buckets from priceOrigin (26:280) · +/- = price zoom (14:1214)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: (heuristic) Pulled liquidity is an inference from L2 changes, not an observed cancel. The event is typed as estimated, and the story's caveat says so; a mark that reads as fact overclaims, and a description that implies intent overclaims more.

kids.name: value
kids.chars: "(estimated) a level dropped without matching prints" (24:620) · "without L3 data replenishment is inferred from L2 changes only" (11:2143) · "Cluster disappeared without a matching traded volume (spoof-ish behaviour)" (24:1269)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: (heuristic) The probe "what just got pulled?" fails unless a pulled level looks different from a consumed one: both are a level that shrank, and only the prints at that price tell them apart. Hue alone cannot carry the difference (05 §4).

kids.name: value
kids.chars: "a level removed without matching trade prints at that price within the window" (E21.json:853) · colour is never the only channel (05:107)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: (heuristic) The design system already has a proposed pattern word for this: hollow, dashed or hatched means estimated or absent. Reusing it for "pulled" keeps one meaning per pattern across the product.

kids.name: value
kids.chars: "Hollow, dashed or hatched = estimated or absent, never a side or direction." (E25D01:334) · "Pulled-liquidity shading on the heatmap surface for levels removed without matching prints" (E21.json:678)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: (heuristic) 200 is already the shipped tier and the accepted ADR's default; 500 is behind a flag that is off, and the deep-book cap may refuse it. A default other than 200 would contradict shipped code.

kids.name: value
kids.chars: DEFAULT_DEPTH = 200 (tiers.py:18) · "Decision: defer — default depth 200 (200@100ms) for all symbols." (ADR21:120) · "500 only with heatmap_depth_500 on" (23:747)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: (heuristic) A step down from 500 to 200 loses more than "rows": the far walls beyond the tier, the cumulative depth beyond it and the heatmap rows outside it; on a mid-cap symbol the ADR measured the difference. A notice that says only that depth was reduced leaves the trader to guess.

kids.name: value
kids.chars: "49 ticks/side for a mid-cap symbol like SOLUSDT, vs. 123 at tier 500" (ADR21:121–122) · cumulative depth column (05:188)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: (heuristic) Four texts disagree on what is shed first and who decides (C6). The one constant is the story's NFR: never silent.

kids.name: value
kids.chars: "never silently degrade without telling the user" (11:2068) · "heatmap cadence and trail are shed before depth" (E21.json:624) · "applied only on the user's click" (14:3114)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: (heuristic) The live trail the panel can draw at full resolution is 60 s: the GPU ring holds 600 frames at 100 ms. Longer spans need the coarse ring, a different resolution the trader should be told about.

kids.name: value
kids.chars: "heatmap trail keeps ≤600 frames in a ring buffer on the GPU" (14:1218) · trail [60s v] header default (14:1197) · the coarse ring at 1 column per second (26:278)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: (heuristic) The probe "which row is yours?" is a column question: the story and the component both want a dedicated own-order column in text, so it never depends on a glyph drawn on the canvas or on a colour.

kids.name: value
kids.chars: "that row shows my order size in a dedicated own-order column with an identifying glyph" (11:2079) · the "Your orders" column (15:2966) · the "My orders" column (05:189)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: (heuristic) A keyboard user cannot predict Enter on the ladder: three texts give it three meanings, two of them place an order. On a trading grid that is a Blocker until one model is chosen (C2).

kids.name: value
kids.chars: "supports Enter to open a row action menu" (14:1217) · "Enter=buy (configurable), Shift+Enter=sell" (15:1233) · Place limit at focused row, Enter (05:67)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: (heuristic) The legend must carry the convention in words and the scale in numbers, because the bid/ask hue is user-configurable and the scale may be log.

kids.name: value
kids.chars: "colour scale legend with numeric anchors" (14:1221) · "convention explicitly stated as text" (15:1336)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: (heuristic) Reduced motion turns the trail fade into an instant change; the re-centre should be checked against the same rule (05 names only the trail), and E21-D05 owns the re-centring numbers.

kids.name: value
kids.chars: trail fade replaced with instant state changes (05:216) · "Hysteresis numbers for re-centring (trigger band, target position, minimum interval)" (E21.json:173)

kids.name: value
kids.chars: sees a band end in the trail; must decide whether it traded away or was pulled

kids.name: value

path/value.chars: scans for the own-order cell while the price moves

br/value.chars: breaks if the ladder re-centres every tick (F-2) or the order is a glyph only (F-14)

p/value.chars: P2b, "leans on multi-TF layouts, journal and alerts more than on the DOM" (10:112): "the app just dropped you from 500 to 200 depth — what did you lose?"
